paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this passage is teaching. God is serious about the way people live, and He is not hiding it. The LORD says the Day of the LORD is "near—near and coming quickly" (Zephaniah 1:14). A warning this loud is not meant to scare you for fun. It's meant to wake you up before it's too late.

Look at who the LORD points at. He names people who bow to other gods, people who swear by the LORD and also by Milcom, and people who "turn back from following the LORD, neither seeking the LORD nor inquiring of Him" (Zephaniah 1:5-6). Then He names the men settled in complacency, who say to themselves, "The LORD will do nothing, either good or bad" (Zephaniah 1:12). I think that's the one that should make us all sit up straight, because that kind of quiet drifting can happen to anybody. And when the day comes, "Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them" (Zephaniah 1:18). Whatever you're leaning on besides the LORD, friend, it can't hold you up.

So what do you do with a heavy word like this? You take it seriously, and you keep your heart turned toward the LORD, seeking Him and inquiring of Him, the very things those people stopped doing. It's why my ovens stay ready, baker. I don't know when the Day comes, and Matthew 24:36 says only the Father does. So let's keep baking, keep reading the Word, and keep our eyes on Him.
